**Department**

Engineering

  

Small businesses represent 99.9% of all companies, yet they're still forced to choose between clunky, outdated enterprise phone systems or their personal phones. This multi-billion dollar market has been overlooked for decades, left to cobble together solutions that slow them down instead of helping them grow.

  

Quo is changing that. We bring calls, texts, and customer information together into one easy-to-use, AI-powered platform. We're not just building a phone system. We're setting a new standard for how businesses connect with their customers.

  

Driven by our values, we move fast, build with determination, and obsess over delivering value to the businesses that have been underserved for far too long.

  

Today, Quo is trusted by more than 120,000 companies and rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2. We're backed by Y Combinator, Tiger Global, Craft Ventures, Slow Ventures, and other top-tier investors. It's safe to say we're onto something big.

**About the role**
==================

We're looking for a Frontend Engineer to join our Communication squad, part of the Workflow pillar. Communication owns the core of what Quo does: calling, messaging, voicemail, transcription and the workflows that support them. You'll build the interfaces thousands of businesses rely on every day, working alongside product, design, backend engineers and three Senior Frontend Engineers who will support you on architecture while you take on sizeable pieces of work and own them from end to end. This is a role with real room to grow, and we're looking for someone who wants to reach the next level.

**Some of the things you'll do:**
---------------------------------

* Help us re-architect calling and standardize how we work with calling providers.
* Build new dashboards and tooling, and reliability work that gives us deeper observability into calling performance.
* Ship new features and delighters such as URL unfurling, custom transcript summaries, group messaging, direct messages and new calling features.
* Own projects from end to end, with support from senior engineers, and take on more ownership as you get familiar with the platform.
* Enhance existing features, fix bugs and improve documentation across calling, messaging, voicemail and transcription.
* Write your own tests and ship safely through our delivery pipelines.

**Technical stack and tools:**
------------------------------

* Our frontend is a Single Page Application built with React and TypeScript, using GraphQL to talk to our backend
* We develop in a monorepo powered by pnpm and Turborepo
* We use Storybook for component-driven development
* Components are implemented with Vanilla Extract for styles, React Aria, and our existing Design System components
* We write tests using Vitest and Playwright, and ship through CI/CD pipelines
* Real-time messaging and calling use WebSockets and WebRTC
* Other tools: Figma, Heap, Linear, Notion, Datadog and Slack

**About you**
=============

* You have experience working with React and TypeScript
* You understand how data flows from the backend to the frontend, including GraphQL, schemas and the basics of database design
* You write your own tests (we use Playwright) and are comfortable with integration and unit testing
* You enjoy solving problems and collaborating with others to design and build a delightful end user experience
* You have some experience with web performance, observability, and accessibility
* You take ownership of your work and understand the importance of communication. You hold yourself to a high standard and help empower others to do the same
* You are a team player. You're happy to start with bug fixes and documentation to make the team better, you admit mistakes and gaps in your knowledge without shame, and you're quick to back a better idea than your own
* You are proactive and self-driven in a fully remote team. You keep work moving without being chased, pick up the next task when you finish one, and can juggle multiple projects and context switch well
* You know that what you ship is felt by thousands of customers, so you are methodical about testing and quality
* You are intentional about how your work impacts customers, the community, and each other. You practice empathy, generosity, and thoughtfulness as you evaluate tradeoffs in pursuit of the best solution
* You are curious. You seek to understand the 'why' behind things, so that you can better plan and build the 'how'. You don't hesitate to ask questions when necessary. You're a lifelong learner with the drive to grow to the next level
* Your code is a pleasure for your teammates to read and understand and you strive to ensure it is readable, testable, and maintainable. When working in the codebase, you leave things better than you found them
* You embrace AI and are keen to use it deeply in your day-to-day engineering work, rather than shying away from it

**Nice to have:**
-----------------

* Experience with real-time messaging technologies such as WebSockets and WebRTC
* Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines and a mature delivery process
* Experience building with agentic AI workflows (for example, breaking tickets down, generating features, and testing and verifying the output)

**Compensation**
================

The annual base salary range for this position is as follow, plus equity and benefits:

* SF Bay Area, Los Angeles, Seattle, Portland, Boston, New York, and Washington, DC Metro: $170,000 - $200,000 USD
* All other US Locations: $153,000 - $180,000 USD
* Canada: $156,000 - $183,000 CAD

The ranges displayed reflect the target for new hire salaries, and within each range, individual pay is determined by your skills and experience, as well as relevant education. Your recruiter can share more and answer questions about the specific salary range during the hiring process.

Salary is just one component of Quo’s total compensation package. Your total rewards package will include equity, extensive medical coverage, a monthly lifestyle stipend, and a flexible PTO policy.

**Who we are**
==============

  

We're a remote-first company with a culture of trust, autonomy, and action. As we rapidly grow, we're intentionally building communities in a handful of hub cities while continuing to hire great talent wherever they happen to live. If you're looking for a place to do your best work, we'd love to hear from you.

  

And remember, there's no such thing as a 'perfect' candidate. We're looking for optimists with grit and determination, who are excited to face the challenges of a growing startup. Quo is the type of company where you can grow, and we encourage you to apply for this role even if you don't think you meet all the requirements.

  

We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse work environment. It is important that you are able to bring your authentic self to work every day. As a global leader in cybersecurity, CrowdStrike protects the people, processes and technologies that drive modern organizations. Since 2011, our mission hasn’t changed — we’re here to stop breaches, and we’ve redefined modern security with the world’s most advanced AI-native platform. We work on large scale distributed systems, processing almost 3 trillion events per day and this traffic is growing daily. Our customers span all industries, and they count on CrowdStrike to keep their businesses running, their communities safe and their lives moving forward. We're proud to work for a mission-driven company leveraging AI to transform the way we work. CrowdStrikers drive their careers through flexibility and autonomy while also being expected to contribute to a culture of responsible AI adoption, experimentation, and innovation. We use an AI-first mindset as a force multiplier to proactively and continuously accelerate execution, build expertise, uncover insights, and solve complex problems. We’re always looking to add talented CrowdStrikers to the team who have limitless passion, a relentless focus on innovation and a fanatical commitment to our customers, our community and each other. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.

**About the Role:**  
The Falcon sensor is the front line of CrowdStrike's platform. Running as a lightweight agent on millions of endpoints, it observes system activity in real time, stops malicious behavior on the device, and streams telemetry to the cloud, where it's correlated across customers' environments to surface and prioritize threats.

The Core Windows team owns the kernel-mode foundation and user-mode low level system frameworks of the Falcon sensor on Windows: the drivers and event sources that give CrowdStrike deep visibility into file system, registry, process and network activity, and the mechanisms that let the sensor act on that in real time. These components run at the lowest level of the operating system on every Windows endpoint CrowdStrike protects.

As a Senior Engineer II on this team, you'll own the design and development of core capabilities in both kernel and user mode that cut across the major OS subsystems, including memory management. Many of these capabilities share components with the Linux and macOS sensors. Because this code runs on every protected Windows endpoint, performance, stability, and correctness are first-class requirements.

This is a systems software role. You'll work close to the OS, reason carefully about behavior under real-world load, and hold a high engineering bar in a codebase where reliability is non-negotiable. You'll collaborate closely with peer engineers on the macOS and Linux teams, and with many other teams inside and outside the core organization.

**What You're Stepping Into**
-----------------------------

You'll join a tight-knit team of deep Windows kernel and system software engineers with a strong track record of delivering complex, cross-team initiatives without lowering the quality bar. The team's scope is expanding, and it holds a central role in shaping the next generation of the Falcon sensor on Windows. That means real ownership early: you won't be maintaining a corner of the codebase, you'll be helping decide where it goes next.

**What You'll Do**
------------------

  

* Design, develop, and own kernel-mode and lower level system software components of the Windows sensor, from design through delivery and production validation
* Partner on sensor architecture and technical strategy for endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities
* Build software with cross-platform deliverables in collaboration with Linux and macOS engineers
* Drive design reviews and provide substantive code review that raises the bar for the team
* Diagnose and resolve complex production issues and customer escalations, including crashes, hangs, and performance regressions
* Improve the test infrastructure and tooling that keep kernel-mode code reliable as it evolves
* Mentor other engineers and collaborate effectively with multi-functional teams across locations

**What You'll Need**
--------------------

  

* In-depth knowledge of C/C++ and Windows kernel and driver development (e.g., minifilter drivers, kernel callbacks, kernel/user-mode communication)
* Strong low-level Windows OS internals: processes and threads, memory management, the I/O subsystem, and the security model
* Experience debugging memory corruption, deadlocks and resource contention, and system performance problems, including crash dump analysis with WinDbg
* Experience shipping major features and releases as part of a team
* Ability to lead, mentor, communicate, and work effectively in a distributed team
* Willingness to travel occasionally for team offsites and in-person collaboration
* Proven experience utilizing AI technologies to enhance decision-making, streamline workflows and processes, improve efficiency and drive business outcomes.

**Bonus Points**
----------------

  

* Experience with Windows Filtering Platform (WFP), Event Tracing for Windows (ETW), or other kernel-mode telemetry sources

* Strong background in scalable, lightweight, high-performance systems

About the Role:
Notion is looking for an experienced engineer who has designed and built secure software systems to help define the security foundations for our AI products. You’ll work with product and engineering teams on agent runtimes, tool permissions, retrieval, content writes, observability, and abuse-resistant design. You’ll turn product risks into clear architecture, reusable guardrails, automated tests, and production systems that help teams ship new features safely.
This role is based in San Francisco. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days.

Translate threat models for new product surfaces into concrete engineering requirements, production checks, and launch criteria.

Help define the security bar for how engineers use coding agents, MCP-enabled tools, hooks, and internal automation without introducing new risk.

You have 8-10+ years of experience designing, building, or securing complex software systems, and you are comfortable working in production code with product and platform engineers.

Security product strategy:
You can turn a complex security risk you see into a product design or architecture that can be built.
Builder mindset:
You’d rather leave behind a useful tool, test, library, or pattern than a task or project for someone else to pick up later.

Experience building or securing products with tool use, retrieval, workflow automation, content writes, or complex permission boundaries.
Hands-on experience with prompt-injection testing, red teaming, model behavior evaluation, or abuse-resistant application design.
Experience with enterprise SaaS security models: permissions, sharing, audit logs, data residency, encryption, compliance, or customer-facing trust guarantees.
Experience building developer tooling, CI checks, coding-agent workflows, MCP integrations, or internal frameworks that shape how engineers build software.
Public security research, vulnerability writeups, conference talks, or open-source work related to product security or secure developer infrastructure.
